To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the performance of magnesium based rechargeable cells is limited by the formation of an interphase layer on the anode surface, and that the interphase layer is formed due to the reaction between Mg and the electrolyte solution.
(1) the structure of the electrolyte solution is crucial for the performance of the battery; and (2) anode materials that are not Mg-based are not necessarily inferior to Mg-based anodes.

1) Mg2+ is a spectator ion in the electrolyte solution, which is a key finding in the field of secondary magnesium batteries; 2) the anode/e lectrolyte interface plays a major role in the electrochemical performance of the battery; 3) the anode surface is covered with a passivation layer that is composed of a mixture of Mg2+, Cl−, and organic moieties; 4) the passivation layer is not a solid electrolyte
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of electrolyte solutions for rechargeable Mg batteries.
understanding the nature of the anode/electric double layer/electrolytic solution interface.
the development of a new class of electrolyte solutions for secondary magnesium batteries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of secondary magnesium batteries is still far from being satisfactory.
the anode electrolyte solution interfaces in secondary magnesium batteries are far from being understood, but the field is moving forward at a rapid pace.
we still do not have an electrolyte solution that is stable enough towards Mg deposition and dissolution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the anode/electronlyte interface in secondary magnesium batteries is not well understood.
the anode/electric double layer interface in magnesium based batteries is still not fully understood.
the performance of secondary magnesium based batteries is still limited by the anode interface, which is the focus of this review.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anode/electric double layer interface is the main source of the poor performance in secondary magnesium batteries.
the anode/e lectrolyte solutions interfaces in secondary magnesium batteries is a key factor in the performance of such systems.
there is a need for new anode materials and electrolyte solutions that would be compatible with each other and that would enable the development of practical rechargeable magnesium batteries.
